Does the job for desert hiking. Not the lightest, not the heaviest, not the cheapest. Perfectly adequate is the whole review.

I'm the person my whole friend group asks before buying gear, so I test things properly before recommending them. The Packrat Stuff Sack Set got the full treatment: weighed it against the spec sheet (accurate), used it for staying organized in genuinely bad conditions, loaned it to my most destructive friend for a weekend, and inspected every seam afterward. Verdict: my pack went from chaos to a filing cabinet, the drawcord survived my friend, and the finish quality is a tier above the price point. It's going on the shortlist I send people, which currently has four items on it. That's the review. Ask my group chat if you think I'm easily impressed.
Pairs perfectly with my Overlook 10x42 Binoculars — that combo has become my default kit for navigation. It nails GPS tracks even under heavy canopy.
1 star. Nothing wrong with it. It's a sitting cloud after a 20-mile day. But my ex has this exact one and now I can't take mine out without thinking about them. Company should have warned me.

Long review because this thing earned it. I put the Alpenglow Sun Hoodie through a full season: an April trip where it rained sideways for two days, a June traverse with more scrambling than trail, and an August heat wave that melted the parking lot. It never once became the story, which is exactly what you want from gear. I stayed cool at 95 degrees in full sun, and the thumb loops in particular is the kind of detail you don't appreciate until you've fumbled with a worse one in the dark with cold fingers. My hiking partner started the season making fun of how much I paid and ended it asking for the link. I have exactly zero notes for the design team, and I always have notes.

This review has taken me three drafts because I keep changing my mind, so I'm just going to show my work. Reasons to love the Cascade 65 Backpack: it carries 40 pounds like it's 25, the weight is honest, and after a full season of week-long trips it mostly looks new. Reasons I have screamed into the void: the frame stay poked through the back panel, roughly two months in, on a trip where I could least afford it, and the repair ate an evening I'd budgeted for sitting by a lake doing nothing. So where does that leave us? I've already packed it for my next trip, which I suppose is the real rating. But I also packed a repair kit specifically for it, which is the asterisk. Recommended, with eyes open.
